posts.title: A daily report for paid ad campaigns
posts.promise: Turn campaign metrics into a reviewable daily report and alerts.
posts.whatItIs: This is an n8n workflow template for checking Google Ads campaigns each day. It retrieves clicks, impressions, conversions and costs, applies configured scoring rules, records results in Google Sheets, and sends alerts and email reports. A beginner version could handle one account and report metrics without changing campaigns.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: a small marketing agency or business managing paid ads might pay to save time on routine reporting. The source does not establish that buyers have paid for this specific service.
loop: Fetch campaign metrics from an authorized Google Ads account.
Compare metrics with thresholds chosen by the account owner.
Write the results to a Google Sheets log.
Send a summary and flagged items to the team.
Have a person review findings and decide whether to change ads.
posts.evidence: The n8n template page describes a daily Google Ads workflow with metric retrieval, scoring, Sheets logging, Slack alerts and email reports, and provides setup requirements. These are template-page claims, not independent proof of deployment, performance or customer outcomes.
posts.uncertainty: The example is an n8n workflow, not evidence that the original maker has paying customers. The small student version would need authorized ad-account access and should report or alert only; a person must validate benchmarks, recommendations and any budget or campaign change.
first24Hours: Create an n8n test workflow with a manual trigger and sample campaign rows.
Build a daily summary in a spreadsheet using clearly labeled sample data.
Ask one ad manager to review whether the metrics and alerts are useful before requesting account access.

ease.reason: The documented template gives setup steps and a 15–25 minute estimate; credentials and integration knowledge remain hurdles.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: agencies or small paid-ad teams may pay for daily reporting; the source does not establish demand.

feasibility.reason: A one-account read-only report with daily metrics is a plausible two-week build; OAuth/API setup may take longer.

autonomy.reason: The described schedule fetches, scores, logs and alerts repeatedly; a person must review advice and decide campaign changes.

evidence.reason: The first-party template documents a workflow and configuration; it does not prove independent use or results.

steps.message: Assessed all 12 selected leads. Proposed one read-only daily PPC reporting workflow at a provisional mean of 6.0; rejected the other leads for access limits, insufficient product evidence, excessive scope, or no bounded beginner loop.
